title: Faith alone means living efficacious faith as sole instrument
source_text: XXV. Denique quando dicunt nos fide, & quidem sola, justificari, intelligunt fidem vivam & efficacem per bona opera, minime vero fidem mortuam atque otiosam, esse solam conditionem, quam Deus a nobis exigit, ut per Christum simus participes remissionis peccatorum, Deoque ad vitam aeternam accepti: sive solum & unicum ex parte nostra instrumentum, quo tantum beneficium percipimus & apprehendimus; quae certe omnia tantae sunt veritatis & evidentiae, ut citra calumniam exposita atque intellecta, a nullo cum aliqua specie negari possint, imo de illis nobiscum, quoad rem ipsam, consentiant Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores, sicuti jam aliquot Disputationibus manifestum fecimus.
pass_a_gloss: Finally when they say that we are justified by faith, and indeed by faith alone, they understand living and efficacious faith through good works, by no means dead and idle faith, to be the sole condition which God requires of us that through Christ we may be partakers of the remission of sins and accepted by God unto eternal life: or the sole and only instrument on our part by which we receive and apprehend so great a benefit; which things certainly are of such truth and evidence that, when set forth and understood apart from calumny, they cannot be denied by anyone with any show of reason; nay, concerning them as to the thing itself the Doctors of the Roman Church agree with us, as we have already made manifest in several Disputations.
pass_b_english: Sola fide means living, work-bearing faith—not dead idle faith—as sole condition/instrument.
Romans agree on the thing itself when calumny is stripped away.
